disposition_reason: Bangladeshi study of arsenic and nine other elements by ICP-MS in two cultivated oyster mushroom species (n=40 each) from two growers and five market mushroom powders; species statistics in Table 1, site means and market ranges in the text.

study.design: Grower sampling of two cultivated Pleurotus species with paired rice-straw substrate, plus a small market basket
study.origin: Mushroom Development and Extension Institute, Savar (Dhaka) and a private farm in Gazipur, Bangladesh; grown on rice straw
study.market: Powdered mushroom bought in local markets in Dhaka and Gazipur
study.method: Microwave HNO3 digestion, ICP-MS (Agilent 7500ce); arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS after TFA extraction

controls.control: Grower site (Savar, near highways, industry and brick kilns, versus Gazipur, rural)
controls.outcome: Arsenic 0.62 (Savar) vs 0.38 mg/kg dw (Gazipur), p<0.001; cadmium 0.28 (Savar) vs 0.49 mg/kg (Gazipur), p<0.001; mercury 0.15 vs 0.11 mg/kg, p<0.001

controls.control: Species choice (Pleurotus high-king vs P. ostreatus)
controls.outcome: Lead 0.40 (high-king) vs 0.22 mg/kg dw (ostreatus), p<0.05; arsenic at Savar 0.76 vs 0.49 mg/kg; cadmium at Savar 0.22 vs 0.34 mg/kg

controls.control: Market powder vs fresh grower samples
controls.outcome: Arsenic 0.22 (market) vs 0.50 mg/kg (farm), p<0.01; mercury lower in market; cobalt 0.081 vs 0.012 mg/kg
